title: Python language adapter
description:
Add Python language support via tree-sitter-python. See docs/adding-languages.md for the full sketch.

Key work:
- Parser: functions, classes/methods, decorators, module-level assignments
- Import resolution: import/from-import statements, relative imports via __init__.py package detection
- Complexity: add "python" branches to classify_cognitive (including comprehensions)
- FCA attributes: is_async, has_decorator, decorator:X, is_classmethod/staticmethod/property, has_type_hints, returns_none, is_generator, has_dataclass — decorators are especially rich FCA signal
- Effect patterns: fs (open), net (requests), db (cursor.execute), io (print/logging), process (subprocess)
- Flags: pytest (test_*), unittest (TestCase), framework entrypoints
- Module boundary strength: Weak

Estimated effort: ~6 days. Higher ecosystem value than C but noisier call graph due to dynamic dispatch.

Risks: name-based reference resolution produces false positives, dynamic imports invisible, metaclass/descriptor edges invisible.

acceptance_criteria.text: Parser extracts functions, classes/methods, decorators, and module-level assignments as symbols with correct SymbolKind (Class for classes, Function/Method for defs)
References classified with correct RefContextKind (Call, FieldAccess, TypeUse) including method-call disambiguation (foo.bar() → Call not FieldAccess)
Import statements (absolute and relative) extracted as ExtractedImport with raw_path and level
Import resolver resolves absolute imports via __init__.py package tree, relative imports via level-based directory walk, with .sutra/rules.toml override for src-layout projects
Complexity scoring handles if/for/while/try/except, boolean_operator (and/or), conditional_expression, and comprehensions (flow break, no nesting)
FCA attributes include is_async, decorator:X (dotted names without args), has_type_hints, is_generator, returns_none
Effect patterns fire for unresolved external calls (open, requests.get, subprocess.run, etc.) via name-only fallback in enrich_with_effects
Flags detect pytest (test_* functions, @pytest.fixture) and unittest (TestCase subclass) test code
All existing tests pass; new integration tests cover Python-specific parser, resolver, complexity, and FCA behavior

decisions.rationale: Class variant exists and is used by Dart. Python classes are semantically closer to Dart classes than C structs.
decisions.rejected: SymbolKind::Struct — technically works but semantically misleading for kind:struct in FCA queries
decisions.title: SymbolKind for Python classes

decisions.rationale: ALL_CAPS convention is near-universal in Python. typing.Final too rare to detect reliably without import context.
decisions.rejected: All as Static (loses const/mutable distinction); Final detection (requires import context analysis)
decisions.title: Module-level assignment categorization

decisions.chosen: Dotted name, no arguments — decorator:pytest.fixture, decorator:app.route
decisions.rationale: Bare name alone loses context (@app.route → decorator:app is useless). Arguments too specific for FCA lattice patterns.
decisions.rejected: Bare name only — loses valuable dotted context like pytest.fixture vs pytest.mark.parametrize
decisions.title: Decorator extraction granularity

decisions.chosen: __init__.py scan + .sutra/rules.toml [python] package_roots override for src-layout projects
decisions.rationale: Matches Python's own package discovery. Handles traditional layouts zero-config (confirmed on varuna360-core flat layout). Config hint handles src/ layout without fragile pyproject.toml parsing.
decisions.rejected: pyproject.toml auto-parsing — fragile, many build backend formats; __init__.py only — fails for src-layout
decisions.title: Import resolver package root discovery

decisions.chosen: Flow break, no nesting increment — (true, false) in classify_cognitive
decisions.rationale: Comprehensions add mental load but are syntactically flat. Nested comprehensions score correctly via multiple flow breaks without artificial inflation.
decisions.rejected: Flow break + nesting (inflates nested comprehensions); Skip (underweights cognitive load)
decisions.title: Comprehension cognitive complexity

decisions.chosen: Not counted in either cyclomatic or cognitive complexity
decisions.rationale: with is a scope guard, not a branch or decision point. Neither SonarSource nor McCabe count it.
decisions.rejected: Count as (true, true) in cognitive — would inflate scores relative to equivalent non-with code
decisions.title: with statement complexity

decisions.chosen: Extend is_logical_operator to recognize Python's boolean_operator node kind
decisions.rationale: Keeps complexity logic centralized in the shared helper. Python's and/or use boolean_operator nodes with operator field containing 'and'/'or', not binary_expression with &&/||.
decisions.rejected: Match directly in walk_cyclomatic Python arm — duplicates boundary detection logic
decisions.title: boolean_operator handling in complexity

decisions.chosen: Name-only fallback on unresolved call refs in enrich_with_effects (cross-cutting)
decisions.rationale: Python's effectful calls are almost entirely to external packages (open, requests, subprocess). Resolved-only matching would produce zero effect attributes. The fallback also retroactively improves C effect coverage for stdlib calls like fopen/printf.
decisions.rejected: Resolved-only (effects non-functional for Python); Separate Python-only pass (two enrichment code paths)
decisions.title: Effect patterns for unresolved external calls

decisions.rationale: Python has no module-level enforcement. __all__ is advisory. Convention-based visibility (_prefix) same as C.
decisions.rejected: Moderate — would imply Dart-level enforcement that Python doesn't have
decisions.title: Module boundary strength

execution_record: Completed across 4 phases (arc): parser+adapter (sutra/187, done), complexity+effects (sutra/188, done), import resolver (sutra/189, done), integration tests (sutra/190, done). 15 integration tests, 233 resolved imports on libaditya (74 files), 843 on varuna (213 files). Full pipeline works end-to-end: parse → resolve imports → graph → complexity → FCA → effects."
